parsedVerdict.reasoning: PlaceOrderUseCase is a standard application-layer use case, and nothing in it belongs to another layer. execute() turns the command into domain objects (OrderLine.of, Order.place). It gets products through EntityLookupService. It hands the stock-reservation rule to the domain service StockAllocationService. It saves through abstract repository ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository). Finally it maps the result to a DTO with toOrderDto. The file has no persistence code (no SQL or ORM calls), no transport or framework code (no HTTP, decorators or request objects), and no inline business rules. Business decisions stay in domain objects and the domain service. The promise that nothing is stored if a line can't be reserved comes from call order: reserve runs before any save. That is orchestration, which is the application layer's job. The class creates StockAllocationService itself with 'new' instead of having it injected. That affects dependency injection, not which layer owns the responsibility.
